samples.summary: Remembered headingLevel survives a block merge, so a bullet that now holds only body text can un-list into a heading
samples.evidence: `applyMergeBlocks` (block-helpers.ts:271) returns `cloneBlock(block)` for the surviving block, keeping every attribute including the new `headingLevel` memory; the Yorkie merge path likewise keeps the first node's attributes. Sequence: bullet a Heading 2 (block now `list-item` + `headingLevel: 2`), delete its text, then Backspace at the start of the following plain bullet (`Doc.deleteBackward` -> `mergeBlocks`, document.ts:289). The merged bullet now contains only the *following* item's body text but still remembers level 2, so `unlistedBlockType` (types.ts:340) turns that body text into a Heading 2 on the next Enter/Backspace/toggle exit. The new test file explicitly guards the symmetric split direction ('the memory belongs to the block that was bulleted', list-heading-roundtrip.test.ts) but nothing clears the memory on merge.

samples.summary: Enter at offset 0 of a non-empty bulleted heading leaves the heading memory on the emptied bullet, and the bullet that carries the text loses it
samples.evidence: `applySplitBlock` builds `before = cloneBlock(block)` (keeps `headingLevel`) and deletes `after.headingLevel` when `newBlockType !== 'heading'` (line 256-258); `Doc.splitBlock` picks `newType = 'list-item'` for list items (document.ts:330). With offset 0 the *text* moves into `after` (which loses the memory) while the now-empty `before` keeps it. So pressing Enter at the start of a bulleted 'Quarterly results' and then un-bulleting the text gives a paragraph, while the stray empty bullet above restores a Heading 2 — the inverse of the intended behavior. The Yorkie path (yorkie-doc-store.ts:2139) behaves the same way.

samples.summary: `unlistedBlockType` keys on the mere presence of `headingLevel`, not on the block having been a heading, so any residual level promotes a bullet to a heading
samples.evidence: `if (block.headingLevel !== undefined) return { type: 'heading', ... }` — there is no check that the block ever was a heading, and no clamping of the level. Producers that set `headingLevel` on a block whose type is assigned separately (paste head/tail metadata copy at text-editor.ts:3578 and :3607, clipboard `makeBlock` at clipboard.ts:108, docx import at docx-importer.ts:242 where the level may be 7–9 from Word) can leave a level attached to a non-heading block; bulleting and un-bulleting such a block then yields a `heading` with a possibly out-of-range `headingLevel` (only clamped later inside `blockStyleId`).
searchedFor: grep headingLevel across packages/docs/src and packages/frontend/src

samples.summary: Un-bulleting now changes the named style id (normal -> heading-N), which re-materializes spacing and discards block spacing the user set while the block was a bullet
samples.evidence: memory.ts:272 `if (blockStyleId(block) !== prevStyleId) block.style = materializeBlockSpacing(...)`, and the same in yorkie-doc-store.ts:1404. Before this change the list exit produced a `paragraph` ('normal' both sides), so spacing/lineHeight set while bulleted survived; now the exit produces `heading-N`, whose style-owned marginTop/marginBottom/lineHeight overwrite the block's values. Round-tripping bullet on/off on a heading with customized spacing therefore silently resets that spacing.

finding.summary: Remembered headingLevel survives a block merge, so a bullet that now holds only body text can un-list into a heading
finding.evidence: `applyMergeBlocks` (block-helpers.ts:271) returns `cloneBlock(block)` for the surviving block, keeping every attribute including the new `headingLevel` memory; the Yorkie merge path likewise keeps the first node's attributes. Sequence: bullet a Heading 2 (block now `list-item` + `headingLevel: 2`), delete its text, then Backspace at the start of the following plain bullet (`Doc.deleteBackward` -> `mergeBlocks`, document.ts:289). The merged bullet now contains only the *following* item's body text but still remembers level 2, so `unlistedBlockType` (types.ts:340) turns that body text into a Heading 2 on the next Enter/Backspace/toggle exit. The new test file explicitly guards the symmetric split direction ('the memory belongs to the block that was bulleted', list-heading-roundtrip.test.ts) but nothing clears the memory on merge.

verdict.reason: The claimed code and path both exist. `applyMergeBlocks` (block-helpers.ts:271-276) clones the first block wholesale and only overwrites `inlines`, so `headingLevel` survives a merge, while the symmetric `applySplitBlock` (block-helpers.ts:256-258) explicitly deletes it. `MemDocStore.setBlockType` (memory.ts:249,257-260) is what puts `headingLevel` on a `list-item`, and `applyDeleteText` (block-helpers.ts:127-141) does not clear it when the bullet's text is deleted. `Doc.deleteBackward` only un-lists when *the current* block is empty (document.ts:264); a following bullet that has text falls through to `mergeBlocks` at document.ts:289 -> `MemDocStore.mergeBlock` (memory.ts:233-240), leaving a surviving block whose text came entirely from the next item but which still remembers level 2. `unlistedBlockType` (types.ts:337-344) keys only on `headingLevel !== undefined`, so the next Enter/Backspace/toggle exit (document.ts:267-268, 304-305) promotes that borrowed body text to Heading 2. I enumerated all merge call sites (memory.ts:233, store.ts:106, document.ts:289/348, text-editor.ts:1913/1959/1984/2030/3166/3268/3334, yorkie-doc-store.ts:2160) and none clears the level, so no existing guard makes it unreachable. The plan's own non-goal (todo.md:53-57) accepts only the split direction and states the invariant that only the block actually bulleted should remember, so merge retention is not sanctioned intent. Real, reachable, unguarded -> stays in the gate.
